unsupported_claims: w = 10 and t = 40 match the defaults used in the original DeepWalk work, which reported good performance with them
The authors fixed these values to hold a known-good configuration constant
Fixing them avoided an expensive combinatorial search over every parameter

rationale: The evidence says the values were chosen as sensible ones that emphasize local structure, after which dimensionality, walks per vertex, and training data were varied. The answer misses the local-structure rationale and invents unsupported claims about original-paper defaults, avoiding combinatorial search, and varying the learning rate, though isolating the effect of other parameters is loosely consistent with the evidence.
